WRONG WORD — the label names a different thing from the picture. SAOL: 'mikro|våg substantiv ~en ~or' = 'ytterst kortvågig ELEKTROMAGNETISK STRÅLNING' — the RADIATION. The appliance is a SEPARATE SAOL headword: 'mikro·vågs|ugn substantiv ~en ~ar' = 'anordning för uppvärmning av mat med hjälp av mikrovågor'. All five images show the appliance, so 'Mikrovåg' read aloud to a child beside a microwave oven names the radiation, not the oven. HOLD rather than FIX because this is a LEMMA change, not a form correction. Recommend: singular 'Mikrovågsugn', plural 'Mikrovågsugnar', gender unchanged (n). Same class as the brief's ängelfisk/kejsarfisk case: a real Swedish word, correctly inflected, attached to the wrong referent.

'Mikrovågor' is the CORRECT plural of the WRONG lemma (SAOL mikrovåg '~en ~or'). It resolves only with the singular above; under the recommended lemma it becomes 'Mikrovågsugnar' (SAOL mikrovågsugn '~en ~ar'). Not fixable independently.

The stored 'Milkshakes' is very likely the GENITIVE SINGULAR, not a plural. NEITHER authority gives a plural: SAOL stops at 'milkshake substantiv ~n [-en]' and SO at 'milkshake milkshaken' — both list only the definite singular. The one source that inflects it, sv.wiktionary, gives plural 'milkshaker' and lists 'milkshakes' explicitly as the GENITIV SINGULAR. So no Swedish authority supports 'Milkshakes' as a plural — but I will not FIX to a form (milkshaker) resting on a single cross-check source that SAOL and SO both decline to confirm. Recommend 'Milkshaker'; needs an operator call.

Picture question. Both images show a STAND MIXER (köksmaskin / köksassistent — a motorised machine with a bowl on a stand), but an 'elvisp' is a HAND-HELD electric whisk. A Swedish cook does not call the pictured appliance an elvisp. Recommend 'Köksmaskin' (pl. köksmaskiner) or 'Köksassistent'. HOLD not FIX — a lemma change, and the operator may prefer either candidate.

THREE faults at once. (1) DEFINITE FORM IN THE SINGULAR FIELD: 'Blomman för dagen' is a fixed DEFINITE phrase ('the flower for the day') — the same defect class as the brief's sv 'Jultomten', and exactly what let the script append -ar. (2) The art shows a hibiscus-type bloom, not a trumpet-shaped Ipomoea. (3) Not a SAOL headword ('Inga träffar på blomman för dagen'). Needs an operator ruling on BOTH the lemma and the art; never rewrite blind.

'Blomman för dagenar' IS A FABRICATED NON-WORD and must not ship under any resolution — the script appended -ar to a definite noun phrase (the Gardinerar/Musklerar class named in the brief). I do NOT rule NO_PLURAL because that would presuppose the phrase-lemma the singular row is holding: if the art wins and the lemma becomes e.g. 'Hibiskus', a real plural (hibiskusar) exists. Resolves only together with the singular.

ONE KEY, TWO REFERENTS. 'Nagel' (SAOL: 'hård del på finger el. tå') names the body_parts art correctly, but the tools art is a hardware nail = SPIK (SAOL '1spik ~en ~ar', 'hammare och spik'). No single Swedish word covers both at child level: Swedish splits precisely where English does not. (SAOL nagel sense 2 does gloss 'spik, bult, nit, plugg', but that is archaic/technical and is not what a Swedish child calls a nail.) Needs an operator ruling: split the key, or drop one theme. Fix the WORD or fix the ART — do not average them.

WRONG LEMMA FOR THE PICTURE. SAOL defines HÅV as 'ett fångstredskap med nät- el. tygpåse' — precisely the hooped, handled implement pictured. SAOL's 'nät' is instead 'konkret: fisknät; slå bollen i nät' — the MESH itself or a fishing/goal net, not a hand net. A Swedish child at the beach carries a håv, not a nät. HOLD (not FIX) because this is a lemma change. Recommend: singular 'Håv', plural 'Håvar' (SAOL 'håv ~en ~ar'), gender n (see the gender row — it must flip).

PICTURE CONTRADICTS THE WORD. 'Fruktträdgård' is an ORCHARD — a whole garden/plantation OF fruit trees. The art shows ONE apple tree. A Swedish child shown this picture and told 'fruktträdgård' learns the wrong scope. Recommend either 'Äppelträd'/'Fruktträd' (pl. -träd; NB gender would flip n -> t) or new art showing several trees. HOLD — needs an operator ruling on word-vs-art; do not rewrite blind.

Two independent defects, neither a form fix. (1) UNFLAGGED LEMMA MISMATCH — the picture is a palett (+ pensel), not a painting; same class as the brief's 'singing = a MICROPHONE', and it duplicates the 'palette' key's art. (2) INTERNAL CONTRADICTION — the singular field holds the VERB infinitive 'Måla' (SAOL: 'måla verb ~de ~t') while the plural holds the NOUN 'Målningar' (SAOL: 'mål·ning substantiv ~en ~ar'). A verb cannot be the singular of a noun. Operator must rule: fix the WORD (→ Målning if the art is replaced; → Palett if the art stays) or fix the ART.

Contingent on the singular ruling. IF the lemma resolves to the noun Målning, SAOL 'mål·ning ~en ~ar' → Målningar (i.e. the stored plural is already the correct plural of a word that is not in the singular field). IF re-cut to the pictured object: Palett → Paletter.
Both candidate lemmas (målning, palett) are utrum, so n would hold either way — but the field cannot be ratified while the singular is a verb.

No art (noImage: true) and the row is internally incoherent: type is null, countable is null, and the singular field holds a VERB infinitive 'Leka' (att leka = to play) while the classification asserts countable-thing / hasGender / hasPlural. A verb cannot carry a noun's gender or plural. With no picture there is no way to decide whether the intended sense is the activity (lek), a theatre play (en pjäs), or the verb — and the EN gloss 'Play/Plays' is itself ambiguous across all three. Per the brief a genuine content question is legitimate HOLD; rewriting blind would manufacture exactly the garbage this commission deletes.

Contingent on the singular ruling. The stored plural 'Leka' is the same verb infinitive repeated — not a plural of anything. The candidate resolutions differ completely: lek→lekar (game/play activity) vs pjäs→pjäser (theatre play).
The field asserts n on a verb infinitive. Cannot be ratified until the lemma is decided; both candidate nouns (lek, pjäs) happen to be utrum, but that is not a reason to bless the current row.

Lemma question, not a form fix. 'Keramik' names the MATERIAL/craft (SAOL: 'keram·ik [-i´k] substantiv ~en — framställning av produkter av plastisk lera (porslin m.m.); äv. om motsvarande konstart'). You cannot point at this vase and say 'en keramik'; the Swedish for the pictured object is 'Vas' or 'Kruka'. This also contradicts the classification (countable-thing): a mass/craft noun has been assigned to a picture of one countable vessel. Operator must rule — fix the WORD (→ Vas) or fix the ART.

Contingent, and the row is internally contradictory as it stands: SAOL gives 'keramik ~en' with NO plural, yet the classification asserts hasPlural: true. If the lemma resolves to Vas, SAOL 'vas ~en ~er' → Vaser. Rewriting before the lemma is settled would invent a form.

LEMMA MISMATCH. SO defines portmonnä as 'litet fodral i mjukt material för förvaring av pengar särsk. mynt' — a small soft COIN purse/wallet. The picture is a structured HANDBAG with a carrying handle = 'handväska'. A Swedish child shown this and told 'portmonnä' learns the wrong word. Correcting it changes the lemma (portmonnä→handväska), so per the brief I do not rewrite blind. NB the classifier gave no image_seen for this key; I opened it, and a second independent reviewer opened it separately and reported the same handbag.

'Portmonnäer' is the correct plural OF portmonnä (SAOL 'port·monnä ~n ~er'), so the form is not itself defective — it is the plural of the wrong lemma. If the singular becomes handväska the plural becomes handväskor. Blocked behind the singular ruling.

INTERNAL CONTRADICTION, with no art to adjudicate it (noImage). 'Läsa' is a VERB INFINITIVE (SAOL: 'läsa verb läste läst'), but the row's classification says countable-thing / hasGender true / hasPlural true — a noun default misapplied to a verb, and the en side ('Read'/'Reads') has been pluralised as if it were a noun. Any edit needs an operator ruling on what this key IS, not a form fix. Note its twin `reading` carries g=null while this row carries g='n' — the two cannot both be right.

Blocked behind the singular: a verb infinitive has no plural, but the classification demands one. Pluralising 'Läsa' would manufacture exactly the garbage this commission exists to delete (cf. the brief's 'Singen'→'Singens').
g='n' assigns en-ord gender to a verb infinitive, and no image exists to confirm any noun sense. Contradicts sibling `reading` (g=null).

Two independent problems, so no blind rewrite. (1) NAME: 'Kustsekvoja' is not the standard Swedish name — sv.wikipedia's headword for Sequoia sempervirens is 'Amerikansk sekvoja (Sequoia sempervirens) eller redwood', and kustsekvoja appears nowhere in that article, not even as a synonym. It is a plausible transparent horticultural compound, not script garbage — but it is not the attested name. (2) PICTURE: the redwood is a conifer, and the art gives it a broad ROUND DECIDUOUS crown, so the drawing does not depict the species at all. Operator ruling needed on name vs art, jointly with `sequoia-tree`, which has the same two problems.

LEMMA MISMATCH, confirmed against the dictionary and in BOTH themes. SAOL '1klippa — stycke kalt berg'; SO 'hög, brant, bar berghäll' — a klippa is a CLIFF / bare rock face: something fixed and massive that you climb or fall off. The art is a single loose boulder a child could pick up, which is 'en sten' (SAOL: 'sten substantiv ~en ~ar'). A Swedish child shown this boulder and told 'klippa' learns the wrong word. Recommended lemma: Sten / Stenar / n — a lemma change, so flagged, not rewritten.

'Klippor' is the correct plural OF klippa (SAOL '1klippa ~n klippor'), so the form is not itself defective — it is the plural of the wrong lemma. Under the recommended lemma it becomes 'Stenar' (SAOL 'sten ~en ~ar'). Blocked behind the singular ruling.

SAOL and SO assign NO gender to inlines — it is entered as plural-only, so there is no en/ett to verify against. The row's classification claims hasGender true; the authority can neither support 'n' nor refute it. A genuine contradiction, not a form error — recording it rather than inventing a gender to fill the field.

INTERNAL CONTRADICTION, with no art to adjudicate it (noImage) — same class as `read`, and worse. SAOL has TWO entries: '1springa substantiv ~n springor' = a long narrow SLIT/crack, and '2springa verb sprang, sprungit' = to run. The intended sense is plainly the verb, yet the row's classification says countable-thing / hasGender true / hasPlural true, i.e. it has been typed as a noun — and the only noun reading of 'springa' is 'slit', which has nothing to do with running. Needs an operator ruling on what this key is, not a form fix.

Blocked behind the singular. A verb infinitive has no plural; the noun homograph's plural would be 'springor' (= slits), which would be actively wrong for a key meaning 'run'. This is precisely how the brief's 'Singen'→'Singens' garbage gets made.
g='n' assigns en-ord gender to what is meant as a verb infinitive; it would only be valid for the unrelated 'slit' noun. Contradicts sibling `running` (g=null).

LEMMA MISMATCH, confirmed in BOTH themes. SO defines sparkcykel as 'ett mindre, tvåhjuligt fordon som drivs genom att man skjuter ifrån med ena foten i marken särsk. anv. av barn' — a child's KICK scooter, DEFINED by being pushed along with the foot. Both drawings are motorised Vespa mopeds with an engine, saddle, mirrors and exhaust — a Swedish 'skoter' / 'moped' / 'vespa'. The stored word names a different vehicle from the one drawn, and the SO definition rules it out explicitly. Recommended lemma: Skoter / Skotrar / n — a lemma change, so flagged, not rewritten. I opened both themes because of the brief's balloon rule; here they agree, which makes the mismatch certain rather than partial.

'Sparkcyklar' is the correct plural OF sparkcykel (SAOL 'spark|cykel ~n -cyklar', syncope right), so the form is not itself defective — it is the plural of the wrong lemma. Blocked behind the singular ruling.

SAOL and SO assign NO gender to kläder — it is plural-only, so there is no en/ett to verify 'n' against. The row's classification claims hasGender true; the authority can neither support nor refute the stored value. Recording the contradiction rather than inventing a gender.

Same two problems as `redwood-tree`, and they should be ruled on together. (1) NAME: sv.wikipedia's headword for Sequoiadendron giganteum is 'Mammutträd', not 'Jättesekvoja'; jättesekvoja is a transparent, understandable compound (and arguably the better K-3 word) but it is not the standard name. (2) PICTURE: the giant sequoia is a conifer, and the art gives it a broad round deciduous crown — it does not depict the species, and is barely distinguishable from the `redwood-tree` drawing. Operator ruling needed on name vs art.

SAOL gives NO gender for shorts — a plurale tantum, so utrum/neutrum is not defined. The stored 'n' is unsupported: an en-ord would give def.pl. *shortsarna, but SAOL gives shortsEN. Unlike solglasögon there is no Swedish base noun to inherit gender from. Needs an operator convention for gender on plural-only loans, not a blind flip. (Supersedes v1, which called 'n' inert-but-not-wrong without consulting the entry.)

Skära is the correct Swedish for 'sickle' as a word, but the art does not clearly show one: the handle is long and straight, which is a lie (scythe). Picture question, not a form question — and cross-locale (the same art serves all 11 languages). Operator rules: fix the ART (a short-handled hook) and Skära stands, or relabel to Lie/Liar/n. Do not rewrite blind.

The v1 spelling fix (Diskbank→Diskbänk) landed, but the correctly-spelled word names the WRONG OBJECT. SO defines diskbänk as 'arbetsbänk i anslutning till diskho' — a KITCHEN worktop beside the sink basin. The art (both themes) is a bathroom pedestal basin, which SO defines under handfat: 'behållare för vatten (på toalett eller badrum) för tvättning av (främst) händer och ansikte'. Recommended: Handfat — a COHERENT three-field change, since SAOL gives 'hand|fat substantiv ~et; pl. ~': singular Handfat, plural Handfat (zero), gender t. Alternative: tvättställ (SO's own JFR). Another lemma → HOLD.

A verb infinitive has no lexical gender; the stored 'n' is a script artifact. But the row ASSERTS hasGender:true, so this is an internal contradiction rather than a pure form error — the sibling adjective/activity rows correctly carry null. Needs the operator to re-class the imageless verb rows (sit, sleep, stand) rather than a blind null-flip.

CONFIRMS the v1 content HOLD from the image + dictionary. Släde does not name this picture and it collides with the `sleigh` key, which stores the identical word. SO defines kälke as 'ett mindre snöfordon med två parallella medar' (JFR släde) — exactly this art; släde is the larger horse-drawn sleigh, which is what `sleigh` correctly shows. Recommended: Kälke — SAOL 'kälke substantiv ~n kälkar', giving the coherent triple Kälke/Kälkar/n (gender unchanged). Another lemma → HOLD.

CONFIRMS the v1 content HOLD from the image. 'Åka släde' means riding in a horse-drawn sleigh; the picture shows a child on a kälke, for which the fixed Swedish expression is 'åka kälke' (or 'åka pulka' for the plastic kind). Recommended: Åka kälke. Same operator ruling as `sled` → HOLD so the two stay coherent.
Verbs have no lexical gender; 'n' is a script artifact, but the row asserts hasGender:true — an internal contradiction. Bundle with sit/stand for one operator re-class.

CONFIRMS the v1 content HOLD, now settled by SO against both images. Snigel does not name this picture and it collides with the `slug` key. SO is explicit: snigel = 'typ av snäckdjur som SAKNAR YTTRE SKAL'; snäcka = 'typ av blötdjur med ... krypfot och inälvssäck som är skyddad inom ett KALKSKAL' — protected within a shell, exactly this art. Recommended: Snäcka — SAOL 'snäcka substantiv ~n snäckor', giving the coherent triple Snäcka/Snäckor/n (gender unchanged). Two keys with two distinct pictures must not share one word. Another lemma → HOLD.

SAOL, SO and SAOB ALL return 'Inga träffar på sneaker' — there is no singular *sneaker in Swedish; only the plural-only 'sneakers' is a headword (SAOL 'sneakers; pl. ~en'). So this field stores a word the dictionaries do not contain. (v1 called it 'attested though marginal' from memory; the lookup does not support that.) Because the art is ONE shoe, the fix needs a real Swedish singular — en gymnastiksko / en träningssko — not a form tweak. Another lemma → HOLD.

SAOL gives NO gender — plurale tantum. Same class as `shorts`: def.pl. 'sneakersEN' does not support an en-ord reading (*sneakersarna), and there is no Swedish base noun to inherit from (unlike solglasögon ← glasöga). Needs the operator's convention for plural-only loans.

'Snowboard' names the BOARD (an object). v1 defended it by analogy to soccer→Fotboll, but that analogy does not hold here: unlike fotboll, this row's own activity siblings all name the ACTIVITY — skating→Skridskoåkning, skiing→Skidåkning, sledding→'Åka släde' — so 'Snowboard' is the odd one out and breaks the set's shape. Recommended: 'Åka snowboard' (matching the 'Åka …' shape) or 'Snowboardåkning' (matching the '-åkning' shape); the operator should pick ONE shape and apply it across the activity set. Another lemma → HOLD.

Snödroppe is the correct Swedish for 'snowdrop' as a word — v1 confirmed the lemma from memory and stopped there — but opening the art shows the word does not name the picture, and the dictionary's own definition convicts it: SO defines snödroppe as 'en tidig, låg vårört med smala, fårade, grågröna blad och ensam, HÄNGANDE, vit blomma som i knopp liknar en DROPPE' — a single HANGING drop-shaped bell. The picture is an upright flat six-petal flower with an orange eye (it reads as a narcissus/anemone type). Picture question, cross-locale (same art for all 11 languages). Operator rules: fix the ART, or reassign the key.

Sparv is the correct Swedish for 'sparrow' as a word (v1 passed it OK without the art), but the picture does not look like a sparv: an orange-red face-and-breast on a blue-grey back reads as a rödhake (robin). The word does not name the picture. Picture question and cross-locale (same art for all 11 languages) → the operator rules: fix the ART, or relabel to Rödhake/Rödhakar/n. Do not rewrite blind.

v1 passed this OK ('Stekspade = turner/spatula') without the art — but the art is not a turner. SO defines stekspade as 'ett redskap för VÄNDNING av matvara under stekning' — for FLIPPING food. What is drawn is a soft silicone scraper, which SAOL/SO cover under slickepott ('slicke|pott substantiv ~en ~ar', sense 2: '⟨vard.⟩ ett köksredskap'). Recommended: Slickepott — the coherent triple is Slickepott/Slickepottar/n (gender unchanged). Another lemma → HOLD.

This is the 4th-of-July/toys balloon case exactly, and it is why the open-EVERY-theme rule exists: judging from classroom/ alone gives 'OK'; judging from post office/ alone gives 'FIX → Frimärke'. Both are wrong as a single ruling. Stämpel is CORRECT for the classroom art — SO: 'ett handredskap med upphöjt eller fördjupat mönster, som används för märkning av dokument ... genom avtryck med bläck'. It is WRONG for the post office art, which SO defines under frimärke: 'liten (rektangulär) tryckt pappersbit som klistras på postförsändelse och gäller som porto'. One Swedish word cannot name both and no form edit can fix that. Needs an operator ruling to SPLIT the key (or re-theme the art): stämpel = Stämpel/Stämplar/n; frimärke = Frimärke/Frimärken/t (SAOL 'fri|märke substantiv ~t ~n' — note it flips BOTH the gender to t AND the plural to -n). v1 reached the same shortlist from the theme names alone but could not tell which was pictured; the images settle it — BOTH are.
Verbs have no lexical gender; 'n' is a script artifact, but the row asserts hasGender:true — an internal contradiction. Bundle with sit/sleep for one operator re-class.

v1 passed this OK from memory; the lookup does not support it. Spjutrocka has NO entry in SAOL or SO ('Inga träffar på spjutrocka' in both; only SAOB's unrelated 'spjut'). It is a species term (Dasyatis pastinaca), not general vocabulary — and the art carries no species detail, being a generic cartoon ray. The child-level, dictionary-backed word is the generic Rocka: SAOL '2rocka [råk`a] substantiv ~n rockor', glossed 'en fisk'. Recommended: Rocka/Rockor/n. Another lemma → HOLD.

SAOL has NO headword 'taco': it answers 'Inga träffar på taco. Menade du tacos, tack eller tacka?' and carries only 'tacos [tak´os] substantiv; pl. ~en', glossed with a PLURAL gloss 'tunna majsbröd med olika fyllningar' plus the note '– I sammansättn. taco-' (i.e. 'taco-' only as a compound element). So SAOL sanctions 'tacos' as the lemma and does not recognise a standalone 'taco'. Spoken Swedish does say 'en taco' for one shell, so the stored form is not absurd — but choosing between the SAOL lemma and the spoken form is a lemma decision, not a form fix.

Depends on the singular ruling above, and SAOL's notation for this entry is not decidable at face value: 'tacos substantiv; pl. ~en' gives no definite singular and an unexpected '~en' after 'pl.' (contrast 'timer ... ~n; pl. ~', where ~n is the definite singular and pl. ~ the plural). I will not guess between 'tacos' and 'tacosen'. Flagging rather than forcing.

Two problems, neither a form fix. (1) The picture is ONE SLICE, whereas 'tårta' names a whole cake — a Swede would say 'en tårtbit' / 'en bit'. (2) 'Tårta' specifically denotes a layered cream gateau, whereas the pictured pastry-crust-plus-set-filling wedge reads as paj / cheesecake / mördegstårta. Choosing the right lemma (and/or fixing the art) is an operator call. The word 'tårta' itself is well formed — see the plural/gender rows.

The art does not depict a therizinosaurus, and it duplicates the sibling 'stegosaurus' key's art inside the SAME dinosaurs theme — a child meets two near-identical plated quadrupeds under different names. The WORD 'Therizinosaurus' is the correct Swedish form for the animal; either the art or the key must change. Operator call (fix the word or fix the art). Found by opening BOTH images.

The art is a krona, not a tiara: a tiara is an OPEN, semi-circular ornament worn at the front of the head, not a closed circlet. And it duplicates the object of the sibling 'crown' key inside the same accessories theme, so a child meets two crowns labelled 'Tiara' and 'Krona'. The word 'tiara' is fine Swedish (see plural/gender); either the art or the key must change — operator call. Found only by opening BOTH images, exactly the football precedent in the brief.

Genuine picture question. What is drawn is a väckarklocka (twin-bell alarm clock): it has an hour hand AND a minute hand and tells the time of day. A kitchen timer has a single pointer on a 0-60 minute dial and does not tell the time. The kitchen-tools theme makes 'timer' the evident intent, but a Swedish child shown this says 'klocka' / 'väckarklocka'. Either the art or the word needs an operator decision — more than a form fix.

The art shows a groda, not a padda: a toad has dry warty skin, a squat body and short legs, none of which is present. It also duplicates the sibling 'frog' key's creature inside the SAME forest-creatures theme, so a child meets two frogs labelled 'Padda' and 'Groda'. The word 'padda' is correct Swedish for a toad; either the art or the key must change — operator call.

GENUINE SOURCE CONFLICT — flagging rather than forcing, per the brief's own bison precedent. SAOL and SO have NO entry for Uranus ('Inga träffar på uranus. Menade du uran...?' — stated, not fabricated), as expected for proper nouns. The two Wiktionary editions then DISAGREE: sv.wiktionary gives 'Böjningar av Uranus NEUTRUM' (→ t), while en.wiktionary's Swedish section gives 'Uranus c' (common → n, i.e. the stored value). By the brief's own standard two editions agreeing is evidence and one alone is not — here they contradict, so there is no evidence either way. I also checked sv.wikipedia's Uranus article for decisive predicative agreement and found none ('Uranus är den enda planeten...' agrees with 'planeten', not with Uranus). The general rule that Swedish place-names take neuter ('Sverige är stort') points to t, but Uranus is also a Roman deity (a masculine person), which plausibly explains en.wiktionary's 'c'. Needs a native/operator ruling; I will not guess. IMPORTANT: this does NOT carry over to the sibling 'us'/USA row, where both editions AGREE on neuter — see that row.

The row mixes two lemmas and SAOL settles which is which: 'viol·ett' is an ADJEKTIV (n. ~, ~a) — the colour word — while the plural field holds 'Violer', the plural of the NOUN viol (~en ~er, 'en växt'). So the singular field holds an adjective and the plural field belongs to a different, nominal lemma. The classification (countable-thing / hasGender / hasPlural) can only describe the FLOWER, pointing to singular 'Viol'. But the key ALSO resolves to colors/violet@2x.webp, a paint-drop, where 'Viol' is wrong and 'Violett' right. Another lemma + a picture question + an internal contradiction — all three HOLD triggers at once. Operator rules: fix the WORD (→ Viol) or fix/split the ART. Recommend 'Viol' if the flower reading stands.

'Gå' is the INFINITIVE of the verb gå, not a noun. Worse, this row's classification (countable-thing / hasGender:true / hasPlural:true) CANNOT have been read off a picture, because there is no picture — and the row's own `type` and `countable` are both null. Two readings diverge completely: (a) the English noun 'a walk' → 'en promenad' (countable, n, promenader); (b) the activity 'walking' → an infinitive with NO gender and NO plural, which is exactly how every sibling activity key is stored (writing → Skriva, g:null). Another lemma + an internal contradiction + no art to arbitrate. Operator must rule which sense the key is for, and whether art is coming.

Cannot be 'Gå' under either reading: an activity infinitive has no plural at all, and the noun reading pluralises a different lemma (promenad → promenader). Blocked on the singular ruling; I will not guess.

Lemma-dependent, and the stored value is internally inconsistent: if the key stays the activity, gender must be null (as with writing/white/yellow in this same batch); if it becomes 'promenad', n is right. The stored 'n' presumes a noun reading that the singular field does not actually contain.

The word does not name the picture, and SAOL says why in as many words: skift|nyckel = 'JUSTERBAR skruvnyckel' (SO: 'STÄLLBAR skruvnyckel') — a skiftnyckel is BY DEFINITION the adjustable wrench, the one with a screw that widens the jaw. The pictured tool is a fixed-size combination spanner with no adjusting mechanism at all. Same class as the batch-01 finds (singing = a microphone, chess = a chess piece): the plural of the wrong word. The v1 round passed this row as a clean 'control' because it never opened the image. Recommend 'Blocknyckel' — SAOL carries block|nyckel ('ett verktyg'), the exact term for an open-end + ring-end combination spanner — or the generic 'Skruvnyckel' (SAOL: 'verktyg för att skruva runt muttrar o.d.') if a simpler K-3 word is wanted. CONFIRMS THE v1 HYPOTHESIS EMPIRICALLY — v1 reasoned toward röntgenbild but said 'needs an image check'; I did it, and the art IS a plate. The word names the wrong thing: SAOL röntg·en = 'undersökning med röntgenstrålning' and SO sense 1 = 'teknik för undersökning av föremåls inre struktur' — röntgen is the EXAMINATION/technique. The picture is the resulting RÖNTGENBILD. Corroborating evidence that the label, not the classification, is at fault: SO marks röntgen '(knappast plur.)', flatly contradicting this row's countable-thing/hasPlural:true classification — whereas a röntgenbild is countable and pluralises freely, fitting the classification exactly. So the picture and the category agree with each other and disagree with the word. Recommend 'Röntgenbild' (→ Röntgenbilder). Operator rules: fix the WORD or fix the ART.

'Röntgenar' is invented — the script's -ar default — and is wrong under BOTH readings, so it must not survive; but which correction applies depends on the lemma ruling above, so I will not rewrite blind. If the label stays röntgen: SO gives 'bestämd form och plural röntgen' → the plural is 'Röntgen' (zero), never *Röntgenar. If the label is corrected to röntgenbild: the plural is 'Röntgenbilder'. Either way the stored value is deleted; the operator's lemma call picks the replacement.

ESCALATED by re-verify: THE FIX IS DIRECTIONALLY RIGHT BUT MUST NOT SHIP AS WRITTEN — my rule-7 dup scan caught the one thing the first round did not. 'Sjukhuskläderar' is indefensible (the -ar default bolted onto an already-plural noun; SAOB: 'KLÄDER, pl., se KLÄDE'), so it cannot stay. But patching the plural to 'Sjukhuskläder' makes this row ['Sjukhuskläder','Sjukhuskläder','n'] BYTE-IDENTICAL to the sister key 'scrubs' — the ONLY new collision my scan found across all 39 patched keys, and one CREATED by the fix rather than pre-existing. The two keys are different garments: scrubs is what STAFF wear (de OP-Kleidung, es Uniforme médico, nl Operatiekleding) and a hospital gown is what the PATIENT wears. The cross-locale test makes this decisive: ALL 10 other locales give hospital-gown a COUNTABLE singular patient garment with a real plural (de Krankenhaushemd/Krankenhaushemden, fr Blouse d'hôpital/Blouses d'hôpital, es Bata de hospital/Batas, it Camice ospedaliero/Camici, nl Ziekenhuisjas/Ziekenhuisjassen, da Hospitalskittel/Hospitalskitler, no Sykehuskjole/Sykehuskjoler, fi Sairaalatakki/Sairaalatakit) — Swedish ALONE has collapsed a patient gown into plural-only 'hospital clothes', which is precisely why the script had nothing to pluralise. AND the proposal's stated ground is false: 'Removing the invented form is right whichever way the lemma question is settled' does NOT hold — if the lemma resolves to Patientrock the plural is Patientrockar, not Sjukhuskläder, so this fix is not lemma-independent and would entrench the defect behind a duplicate. Operator must rule the lemma (recommend Patientrock/Patientrockar/n, which also resolves the separately-held gender row, since a plural-only noun can carry neither en nor ett). Delete the non-word — but do not ship a byte-identical twin of scrubs.

ESCALATED by re-verify: NO PLURAL IS ATTESTED ANYWHERE, AND THE PROPOSAL'S ANALOGUE IS THE WRONG CLASS. Verified verbatim: 'Inga träffar på iguanodon' in SAOL, SO and SAOB alike — quoted honestly by the proposal. I then went one step further and checked the source the proposal did not cite: sv.wiktionary DOES have an iguanodon entry, but it carries only 'iguanodon u' with NO Böjningar table at all — so the gender (utrum, = the stored n) is corroborated while the plural is attested by nothing, in any source. That leaves the proposed 'Iguanodoner' resting entirely on the cited elektron pattern — and that analogue does not hold: elektron/proton/neutron are -tron/-on words, whereas iguanodon is a Greek -ODON word (sv.wiktionary etymology: 'grekiska ὀδών (odṓn)'). SAOL's actual -odon control is 'mast·odont [-odån´t] substantiv ~en ~er' — Swedish nativises Greek -odon by taking the oblique stem odont- and adding a -T, giving mastodont -> mastodonter. That points at a LEMMA question (Iguanodont -> iguanodonter?), which per the brief is reserved to the operator and is more than a form correction. Both the stored -ar (the script's unmotivated default; the Latin -us rule cannot reach a Greek stem) and the proposed -er are unattested guesses, so this is not 'keep the stored value' — it is 'neither form is sourced; rule it explicitly'. The proposal itself invites exactly this ('Operator may prefer to leave it pending a native/palaeontology-usage check'), and I agree: do not ship an invented plural to children on a pattern argument built from the wrong word class.

pluraliaTantum.why: The singular field holds a PLURAL — the defect class the brief names — but here that is arguably RIGHT, so I am not calling it a FIX. SAOL: 'flinga substantiv ~n flingor / MEST I PL. lätt, tunt stycke av ngt: snöflinga; FLINGOR MED MJÖLK'. A singular flinga exists but means ONE FLAKE, not the breakfast product; SAOL's own example for the food sense is the plural (flingor med mjölk). As the name of the cereal the word has no usable singular, so 'Flingor' in the singular field is the honest label — flagging it as pluralia tantum rather than manufacturing *'En flinga' as a cereal label. Note this also sits oddly with the classification (countable-thing, hasPlural:true) — the picture is a bowlful, not one countable flake.

SAOL: 'pommes frites [påmfrit´] substantiv; pl. ~en' — marked PLURAL, no singular exists. SO agrees: 'pommes frites plural, bestämd form plural pommes fritesen'. The singular field cannot hold a singular; the label is the plural, consistent with the plural-picture classification. SEPARATE DEFECT in the same field: the stored form mis-capitalises the second word. Swedish writes 'pommes frites', not 'Pommes Frites' — cf. the plural field, which already has it right. Whatever is done about the plurale-tantum status, the stored string should read 'Pommes frites'.

SAOL: 'glas|ög·on substantiv; pl.' — marked plural, full stop; no singular form exists. SO: 'glasögon plural'. So the singular field cannot hold a singular. Note also that the classification (countable-thing, hasPlural:true) is contradicted: the object is ONE pair, and the Swedish word has no singular at all. This is the brief's pluralia-tantum-over-one-object case (pants/scissors) — the object is single, the word is plural-only.

'Sjukhuskläder' is a PLURAL sitting in the singular field. SAOL lists 'kläder' as its own headword and SAOB marks it explicitly 'KLÄDER, pl.' — kläder has no singular. Separately surfaced (not rewritten blind): a hospital GOWN is one garment, whereas sjukhuskläder = 'hospital clothes'; the single-garment word is patientrock / sjukhusskjorta. Operator decision on the lemma.

SAOL 'jeans substantiv; pl. ~en' and SO 'jeans plural, bestämd form plural jeansen' — SAOL gives ONLY plural forms; there is no singular *en jeans (Swedish counts it 'ett par jeans'). Separately flagged: the clothing-theme art is knee-length shorts, so the label only names the objects-bw art — a multi-theme divergence of the same kind as the batch-01 balloon.

SAOL 'leggings substantiv; pl. ~en' and SO 'leggings plural, bestämd form plural leggingsen' — SAOL gives ONLY plural forms; there is no singular *en legging (Swedish counts it 'ett par leggings'). Note this is NOT the brief's one-object-pluralia-tantum inverse trap: unlike German Hose→Hosen, Swedish leggings genuinely has no singular, so PLURALIA_TANTUM is right rather than a hidden real singular.

The singular field holds a PLURAL form. SAOL: 'byxa substantiv ~n byxor — mest i pl.' Swedish names this garment only in the plural (ett par hängselbyxor); *en hängselbyxa is not used. The label correctly names the picture — the defect is structural (a plural in the singular slot), not lexical. Contrast the German case the brief cites (Hose→Hosen): Swedish has no usable singular here.

'Inlines' has no singular: SAOL 'in·lines substantiv; pl. ~en', SO 'inlines plural, bestämd form plural inlinesen' — the word is entered as plural only. So a plural-only form is sitting in the singular field. The art makes it worse: the picture shows exactly ONE skate, which is 'en inlineskridsko' (or rullskridsko). This key needs a singular the stored lemma cannot supply — a lemma change, flagged not rewritten.

The head noun has no singular: SAOL 'kläd·er substantiv; pl.', SO 'kläder plural' — kläder is entered as plural only (its singular counterpart is the separate lemma 'klädesplagg', SAOL '~et; pl. ~'). So 'Sjukhuskläder' is a plural-only form sitting in the singular field. Compounded by the art: the picture is ONE garment, which a collective 'sjukhuskläder' (hospital clothing in general) does not name — a single top would be 'ett klädesplagg' / 'en sjukhusskjorta'.

SAOL: 'shorts [ʃå´rts] substantiv; pl. ~en' — PLURAL ONLY, no singular. SO agrees: 'shorts plural, bestämd form plural shortsen'. Swedish sanctions no singular *en shorts (one says ett par shorts). This CONTRADICTS the batch classification (countable-thing / hasPlural true) and per the brief the dictionary wins. Note this is NOT the German Hose→Hosen trap: German has a singular, Swedish genuinely does not.

SAOL: 'sneakers [sni´kers] substantiv; pl. ~en' — plural only; SO: 'sneakers plural'. There is no sanctioned singular (SAOL/SO/SAOB all return no hits for 'sneaker'), so this is genuine pluralia tantum rather than the v1 'borderline' reading. SAOL: 'sol|glas·ög·on substantiv; pl.' — plural only; SO: 'solglasögon plural'. Same for the base: SAOL 'glas|ög·on substantiv; pl.'. Swedish has no singular for spectacles (one says ett par solglasögon).
